# Toronto Tenant Repair Request Checklist

A cooperative repair request works best when it is clear, dated, and well documented. For Toronto tenants, the main goals are to notify the landlord promptly, keep a paper trail, and escalate only if needed.

# Repair Request Plan for Leaking Ceiling and Broken Heater

## Step-by-Step Timeline
| Step | When | What to do | Goal |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Today | Take photos/videos of the leak, ceiling damage, heater issue, and thermostat reading | Create evidence |
| 2 | Today | Send a polite written repair request by email/text | Start the record |
| 3 | Within 24 hours | Ask for a repair date and confirm whether entry is needed | Get a response |
| 4 | Within 2–3 days | Follow up if there is no reply or no appointment | Keep momentum |
| 5 | After 5–7 days, or sooner if heat/water damage worsens | Send a firmer written follow-up with a deadline | Show urgency |
| 6 | If the heater fails in cold weather or the leak spreads | Contact the City of Toronto or the Landlord and Tenant Board for next-step options | Protect habitability |
| 7 | After repairs | Save before/after photos and confirm the fix in writing | Close the loop |

## Polite Message Template
Use this as an email or text message:

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m writing to report two repair issues in my unit: a leaking bathroom ceiling and a broken heater. I moved in on 2025-11-01 and pay CAD 2,150 per month.

The bathroom ceiling appears to be leaking, and the heater is not working properly. I’d appreciate it if you could arrange repairs as soon as possible, since both issues affect the condition and comfort of the unit.

Please let me know when someone can inspect and repair these items. I’m happy to cooperate with scheduling access at a convenient time.

Thank you for your help,
[Your Name]
[Unit Number]
[Phone Number]

## Documentation to Collect
- Photos and short videos of the leak, ceiling staining, dripping, and heater display or lack of heat
- Dates and times when the problem was noticed and when it worsens
- Copies of all messages to and from the landlord
- A note of any temperature readings inside the unit if the heater is failing
- Receipts for any temporary costs if you had to buy a fan, dehumidifier, or space heater
- A simple log of noise, water spread, odors, or any safety concerns
- A copy of your lease and move-in condition notes, if available

## Informal vs Formal Escalation Options
| Option | Best for | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Informal request by email/text | First contact | Fast, cooperative, low conflict | May be ignored |
| Follow-up with a deadline | No response or slow response | Clear, still polite | Can feel firmer |
| Phone call followed by written recap | When you want faster scheduling | Personal and efficient | No record unless you confirm in writing |
| City of Toronto property standards complaint | Ongoing heating or maintenance concerns | Adds pressure through enforcement | Can take time |
| Landlord and Tenant Board application | Serious or unresolved repair issues | Formal legal route | Slower and more involved |
